title: Set a date stamp to the work order's date and stamp it
instruction: Stamp the work order's date in its marked box, then return the stamp to its cradle.
context: Configure, then apply, with a permanent record: the stamp is first set to the work order's date, then used as a tool, inked, pressed once inside the box the right way round, and returned. A wrong setting becomes a wrong impression that cannot be undone, so the scoring rewards configuring before applying. Board tasks that set a device to a value read elsewhere (#746, a clock set from another clock; #237, a busybox set from a setup sheet) end with the configured state; here nothing counts until the setting has been applied. Dated stamps keep receiving, legal and quality records. Done by: shipping and receiving clerks, legal records clerks, quality inspectors.
setup: World x is forward from the arm bases, y left, z up, metres; table top z=0.7475, arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.750). Everything starts upright at yaw 0. Full collider table and seed table in README.md. Date stamp (free; orange ABS custom dater, 258 g: 197 g housing and handle, two 20 g polymer setting wheels, two 3 g spring plungers, 15 g rubber die): root starts at (0.275,-0.417,0.7615), 1 mm above its seat in the cradle. In its own frame: housing box 180x60x45 mm centred (0,0,34.5) mm; post 10x10x27 mm at (0,0,70.5) mm; charcoal rubber handle 30x18x26 mm at (0,0,97) mm. Day wheel at x=+60 mm, month wheel at x=-60 mm: vertical hinges at z=65 mm, -350..+350 degrees, damping 0.00035 N m s/rad, no spring; every joint starts at 0. Hubs are vertical cylinders 54 mm tall centred z=88 mm, radius 12 mm (day) or 22 mm (month). Detents: day 31 steel pins r 1.5 mm on a 20 mm ring, month 12 pins r 3 mm on a 25 mm ring, each pressed by a spring ball plunger (steel ball r 2.5 mm day, POM ball r 5 mm month; 300 N/m, 0.9 N preload). Turning fins: orange day 30x16x22 mm, blue month 44x16x22 mm, centred (wheel x,0,126) mm, long side along x. Wheels and plungers have friction 0.1/0.08. Two ivory 17x13 mm windows on the housing top at (+/-20,-22) mm show the current day and month. Die: dark rubber 40x18x4 mm plate centred (0,0,2) mm on a vertical slide, 0..4 mm travel upward, 800 N/m, 0.8 N preload, damping 2 N s/m, friction 0.6/0.4; its underside carries the mirrored raised DD.MM date (four 10x6 mm seven-segment digits, 1.5 mm segments, centres x=-11.5,-4.5,+4.5,+11.5 mm, decimal square at (0,-4) mm). Cradle (fixed, blue painted steel) at (0.275,-0.417,0.7475): 208x92x4 mm floor; two 180x9x21 mm seat rails centred y=+/-24.5 mm; 4 mm thick, 25 mm tall walls around a 200x84 mm pocket. The seated root is at table +13 mm and the face clears the floor by 9 mm. Ink pad (fixed; black felt in a rigid tray) 90x60x10 mm centred (0.225,-0.290) on the table. Work order (fixed; white cellulose paper taped to the table) 150x130x1 mm centred (0.225,-0.130). Printed on it in its own frame: a blue 120x6 mm header band at (0,57) mm; the requested date as four 24 mm tall dark seven-segment digits DD.MM (3.6 mm segments) centred (0,35) mm; the 80x44 mm marked target box, 1 mm lines, centred (0,-20) mm. Impressions show as ink dots on the sheet (visual only). All parts have friction 1.2 static/1.0 dynamic unless stated, contact offset 0.1 mm. No other props. Layouts, start DD.MM -> requested DD.MM: 0: 03.12->05.01; 1: 11.02->14.02; 2: 24.01->28.03; 3: 29.01->03.04; 4: 10.06->16.05; 5: 23.08->30.06; 6: 05.10->07.07; 7: 18.08->21.08; 8: 04.08->02.09; 9: 21.08->18.10; 10: 31.08->27.11; 11: 14.01->09.12; 12: 31.03->25.01; 13: 17.05->10.02; 14: 06.03->04.03; 15: 25.04->22.04. Layout index = derived reset seed modulo 16; the harness derives zlib.crc32(f"{eval_seed}:{scene_seed}:{epoch}".encode()) & 0xFFFFFFFF. CLI --seed 0 to 17 select layouts 6, 8, 11, 5, 12, 2, 1, 15, 3, 13, 0, 14, 13, 3, 10, 4, 7, 9; no --seed selects layout 3.
scoring: Band reading: day shown = (start day - 1 + round(day angle / (360/31) degrees)) modulo 31 + 1; month likewise modulo 12 with a 30 degree pitch; positive is counter-clockwise seen from above; a band more than 4 degrees from its nearest detent is blank. Inked: face compressed >=1 mm with its centre over the 90x60 mm pad, the bottom of its centre within 2 mm of the pad top and tilt <=10 degrees; ink stays on the face for the rest of the trial. Impression: the inked face compressed >=1 mm with its centre off the pad and the lowest point of its 40x18 mm face (its lowest bottom corner, at any tilt) within 2 mm of the paper top or the table top; dry presses and contacts compressing the face <1 mm leave no impression. Each press makes one impression, recorded at its first sample at >=1 mm: face centre XY, lowest-point height, yaw, tilt, both band readings. The next impression can start only after compression falls below 0.5 mm and the face's lowest point has risen >=3 mm above its lowest height in that press. Smear: before that re-arm, any off-pad contact compressed >=1 mm with the face's lowest point within 2 mm of the paper or table top and the face centre >2 mm from, or yaw >2 degrees from, the recorded impression. Correct impression: both bands nonblank and showing the requested date; face centre on the 150x130 mm work order, the face's lowest point within 2 mm of the paper top; every corner of every active segment and of the decimal square inside the 80x44 mm box with >=5 mm clearance from the inner edge of each 1 mm line; yaw within 5 degrees of the box; tilt <=5 degrees. Zero for the rest of the trial, whatever happens later: an incorrect impression (wrong or blank band, margin, yaw, tilt, off the sheet, on the table; an edge-first press tilted more than 5 degrees is one), a second impression of any kind, or a smear. With no impression, current band credit: 0.15 for each band that needed a change and now shows its requested number; a band whose requested number equals its start number earns 0.15 only while both bands show their requested numbers (layouts 1, 7, 14, 15: 0 until the day is right, then 0.3); untouched start 0 in every layout. Exactly one correct impression: 0.7, whatever the bands show later; 0.9 if also the stamp is tilted <=5 degrees, its whole rotated 180x60 mm housing footprint is inside the 200x84 mm cradle pocket and its root is within 3 mm of its seat height (table + 13 mm); 1.0 if that holds with every gripper TCP >=30 mm from the stamp's bounding box, stamp speed <0.01 m/s, spin <0.05 rad/s, face and both plunger slide speeds <0.05 m/s and both knobs within 1 degree of a detent, all continuously for 1 s. A held or moving seated stamp earns 0.9. Success: 1.0 held for a further 1 s.
reset_notes: Print a fresh work order for the derived reset seed modulo 16 (CLI mapping in setup), set each band's starting offset to that layout's start with every joint at zero, place the upright stamp centred in its cradle 1 mm above the seat, re-ink the pad. Reset clears all impressions, ink, press arming, sticky errors and timers. Keep object jitter zero.
fidelity: Each band's starting number is an offset on its wheel angle, equivalent to the wheel having been turned before the trial; physical detents set the steps. Ink is a visual readout from the face's spring travel and pose, not fluid; the sheet is rigid. Raised die segments and the die carrier are visual only. Primitive ABS housing, polymer wheels, steel pins and passive springs approximate a custom dater. No contact or force readings.
